correctness.rationale: The proof covers all 1<=a<=b and 1<=n<=a+b. Proposition 4.8 of arXiv:1908.05433 covers 2<=n<=a for arbitrary monotone values; n=1 trivial. For n>=b, t=N-n<=a permits injective opposite-part matching for every leftover subset; greedy singleton choices dominate every leftover singleton for every agent, so removal of each recipient’s picked vertex gives EF1_outer. For a<n<b, an R-only singleton exists; unit-additive EF1 forces all bundles to size<=2 and at most a size-2 bundles, contradiction N>n+a. Independent exact-integer checker passed 58546 matching subset tests, 11100 high-band profiles and 116 obstruction parameter instances. The proof, not finite experiments, establishes the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: An exact all-parameter universal spectrum for complete bipartite graph-constrained fair division is a natural classification prompted by the published spectral conjecture, with arbitrarily long missing agent counts and a new sharp high-band constructive guarantee. The core matching argument works for arbitrary heterogeneous monotone nonadditive preferences and ensures EF1_outer, not merely ordinary EF1. The high-band threshold n=b may be arbitrarily far below the previously stated general threshold N-2 when the smaller side grows; the contribution is not a small constant tweak, numerical census or restatement of published lower-range facts.
